# Straight answers — planes, hosts, caps, corrections

> **July 2026 snapshot.** Where this file says "UI-only", "no REST verb" or "walled", read it as a dated verdict:
> many were overturned later (KB `13 - Lessons Learned/Overturned Beliefs.md`, Laws 16-19). Before telling a user
> something is not possible, work the workaround ladder in KB `00 - Start Here/08 New Pipeline Milestones`.
> "Org A" / "Org B" are two example orgs; derive your own values (Law 1).

Look here **before** grepping `content/`. Everything on this page is generated from
`content/*.json`, so it agrees with the master document and the dictionary by construction.

Hosts are written for **Org B** (`<podB>` / `dm-us`). For **Org A** substitute
`<podA>` / **`dmp-us`** — and check the last table first, because several of these planes are
**not mounted on Org A at all**. That substitution is Law 0; getting it wrong 404s silently.

## Auth planes — never mix them

Six planes, six different tokens. The plane is a property of the *path*, not of your login.

| Plane | Login call | Header(s) | Base host | Serves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v2 platform | POST /ma/api/v2/user/login | icSessionId | <pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas | /api/v2/* |
| v3 platform | POST /saas/public/core/v3/login | INFA-SESSION-ID | <pod>.dm-us.informaticacloud.com/saas | /public/core/v3/* |
| Identity / CDGC | identity-service Login, then /jwt/Token | Bearer + IDS-SESSION-ID + X-INFA-ORG-ID | idmc-api.dm-<region>.informaticacloud.com | data360/*, marketplace, MDM control |
| CDGC write plane | same three-header flow | Bearer + IDS-SESSION-ID + X-INFA-ORG-ID | cdgc-api.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | ccgf-*, cdmp-marketplace |
| CAI runtime | v3 session | INFA-SESSION-ID (+ vnd.api+json to publish) | <pod>-cai.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | /active-bpel/* |
| MDM runtime | three-header flow | Bearer + IDS-SESSION-ID + X-INFA-ORG-ID | <pod>-mdm.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | business-entity/public/api/v1/* |
| CDQ dictionaries | either method | Bearer JWT or IDS-SESSION-ID | <pod>-dqcloud-api.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | /quality/public/v2/* |
| Data Profiling | SPA session | IDS-SESSION-ID, SPA-injected | <pod>-dqprofile.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | profiling-service, metric-store |
| MCP servers | three options | IDS-SESSION-ID \| Bearer JWT \| OAuth2 client credentials | a2e-prod-<pod>-mcp.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | /mcp-servers/public/* |
| Anonymous CAI | none | none | <pod>-cai.dm-us.informaticacloud.com | /active-bpel/public/rt/* |

Each row is a documented number. Hitting one of these looks like a bug and is not.

| Service | What is capped | The limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAI | Bulk publish / unpublish | 199 assets per call | Invoke ch.3-4 |
| CAI | Process list default page size | 20 (use listStart + maxReturn to page) | Monitor p.101 |
| CAI | Rate limit | HTTP 429 when requests exceed the window | Invoke p.12 |
| CAI | Activity execution circuit breaker | 10,000 activities -> 429, no new instances for 15 min (tech preview, node-local) | Invoke p.25 |
| CAI | Message payload | 5 MB on Cloud Server; 500 MB multi-byte ceiling | Monitor p.11 |
| CAI | Process timeout / retention | 3,600 s timeout; completed 24 h, faulted 72 h, logs 30 days | Invoke p.25 |
| CDQ | Dictionary shape | Name 125 chars; 42 columns max; column names 64 chars | CDQ API Ref p.7 |
| CDQ | Rows per call | 10,000 (POST and PUT) -> 413 if exceeded | CDQ API Ref p.11 |
| Address Verification | Batch size | 1,000 addresses per call; 100 suggestions interactive | IAV ch.2 |
| Address Verification | Job token | Expires in 5 min; free resubmit 2x interactive / 9x QuickCapture | IAV p.11 |
| Operational Insights | History + concurrency | 13 months (processJobReport), 1 month others; ONE active request per org | OI p.70 |
| Operational Insights | Data retention / refresh | 13 months retained; metrics refresh only once a week | OI p.70, p.110 |
| MDM SaaS | Job concurrency | Queues ingress/egress past 25 per pod or 5 per org | C360 p.247 |
| MDM SaaS | Step queueing | Load >1,000 rows; transform >100,000; index >10,000; match keys >5,000 | C360 p.247 |
| MDM SaaS | File and result caps | CSV 100 MB / 100,000 rows; search page 10,000; export 10,000 | C360 pp.65,168 |
| MDM SaaS | Session | Session ID expires after 30 min of inactivity | vendor deck p.8 |
| Data Profiling | Rule occurrences | Keep at 200 or fewer per profile | CDP p.160 |
| Platform | Token lifetime | JW access token expires 30 min after grant | IAV p.9 |
| MCP | OAuth token timeout | Default 5 min; configurable 5-1440 min | MCP guide |
| CAI | Bulk publish / unpublish | 199 assets per call, processed in payload order | Invoke pp.30, 32 |
| CAI | Unpublish dependency order | Service connector, THEN app connection, THEN process. Wrong order returns per-item ERROR inside a 200 envelope. | Invoke p.35 |
| CAI | REST / SOAP rate limit | HTTP 429 once the rate limit is exceeded in the window | Invoke p.12 |
| CAI | Invocable verbs | GET, POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE on a published process | Invoke p.15 |
| Data Profiling | Rule occurrences per profile | 200 or fewer, else the scorecard job times out | CDP p.160 |
| MCP | OAuth access-token timeout | Default 5 min; range 5-1440 min | MCP guide p.17 |
| MCP | Server scope per OAuth client | Set at creation on the Resources page; editable afterwards | MCP guide p.18 |
| Operational Insights | Concurrency | ONE active GraphQL request per org | OI p.70 |

## Corrections — where earlier conclusions were wrong

Read this before repeating a "we already know X is impossible" claim. Every row is a
belief this project held and then overturned against vendor documentation.

| Topic | What we believed | What is actually true | Why the mistake happened |
|---|---|---|---|
| CAI publish | No REST verb; a human must click Publish. | POST /active-bpel/asset/v1/publish is a documented bulk resource (max 199 assets) and returned 202 with a job ID in testing. Four real processes were published headlessly. | The probed path was asset/publish, not asset/v1/publish — and on the wrong host. |
| CDQ authoring | CDQ has no REST write path at all. | Dictionaries have a complete documented CRUD API on the dedicated -dqcloud-api host. Rules and scoring remain UI-only. | The claim was generalised from rules to the whole service. |
| Data Profiling | Profiling only rides a catalog scan; no API. | Informatica documents create, delete and update for profiles and queries. The paths are in a separate guide not held locally. | Absence of a local document was read as absence of an API. |
| Operational Insights | No REST plane; a gap. | Two documented GraphQL resources at /active-bpel/opsanalytics-das/metrics for CAI job reporting. Not REST, which is why REST-shaped probes found nothing. | Probed as REST on the wrong host family. |
| Scheduling | Native scheduling is UI-only. | POST /api/v2/schedule returns 200 and creates a real schedule. CAI additionally has full schedule CRUD on the restadmin plane. | Never probed before being written off. |
| Data Marketplace | UI-only publish. | Collections, categories, orders, terms of use and delivery targets all create over REST; a full provisioning chain ran end to end. Only the delivery template is UI-only. | Early snapshot never revisited. |
| Mass Ingestion / DBMI | Not provisioned — an entitlement purchase. | Engines RUNNING on both agents with privileges present. Authoring is a UI wizard. Informatica also documents a create endpoint worth re-probing. | 404 responses were read as missing entitlement. |

| CAI provisioning | Not provisioned; zero CAI assets. | 54 to 68 processes deployed and invocable, process engine running. | Same products[] misread, plus an early probe before assets existed. |

## Deploying it — runtime, engines, drivers, sizing

A runtime environment is a **network position**, not a setting: whatever runs your task must be
able to reach your data. Every row below follows from that.

### The three runtime types

| Runtime type | Runs where | Use it when | Cannot |
|---|---|---|---|
| Informatica Cloud Hosted Agent | Inside the IDMC hosting facility. Nothing to install. | Source and target are both SaaS and the connector supports it (check the connector's own guide — support is per-connector). | Reach anything on a private network. It is multi-tenant. A connection bound to it CREATES fine and then cannot see a private host — a 200 that means nothing. |
| Secure Agent group | A host you own and run. | Data is on-premises or on a private network — or SaaS data you do not want going through the Hosted Agent. **The only option that reaches a private database.** | Be avoided if your data is private. You own patching, disk, RAM and uptime. |
| Serverless runtime environment | Informatica-managed compute **inside YOUR OWN AWS or Azure account** — you supply the VPC/VNet, subnets and an IAM role. Vendor wording: auto-scales with the workload 'while your data remains in your cloud environment'. Single-tenant, dedicated VM resources. | Your data is already in AWS or Azure and you want no agent to maintain. | Reach data in any OTHER cloud or datacentre. It is not a general replacement for a Secure Agent — it is an AWS/Azure-native runtime. Also bills IPUs per runtime-hour where an agent is free. |

### Licence, assignment

| State | How you read it | What a failure looks like |
|---|---|---|
| 1. LICENSED | Administrator → Licenses in the UI. There is no licence-inventory API. Privileges are the REST proxy. | Absent from the Licenses page. NOT a 404 from REST — every licence path 404s even when fully licensed. |
| 2. ASSIGNED to an agent | UI: Administrator → Runtime Environments → agent → enable components. **UI-only, no REST verb.** Confirmation string in 53-ui-receipts. | agentEngines[] simply does not contain the engine. A connection test names it exactly: 'No running service found of type <Engine> <ver>.* service for AgentGroup: {reId}'. |
| 3. DEPLOYED / DEPLOYING | GET /api/v2/agent/details/{agentId} -> agentEngines[].agentEngineStatus.status | Status sits at DEPLOYING for many minutes while packages download. Calls keep failing meanwhile, and the engine NAMED in the error changes as each one lands. A moving error is progress, not a new wall. |
| 4. RUNNING and resolvable | Only a PASSING connection test proves this. Nothing else does. | status can read RUNNING in the API while the agent's own log says UNKNOWN and the router still refuses. Under host pressure engines flap RUNNING -> STOPPED. Treat status as a deployment signal, never a completion signal. |

### Third-party JDBC drivers

| Thing | Answer | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical directory for a CCI/JDBC_V2 third-party driver | <agent>/ext/connectors/thirdparty/informatica.jdbc_v2/common/ — Informatica auto-creates it and drops its OWN drivers there (DB2, MSSQL, Oracle), which is how you confirm it is right. | Live 2026-07-26. Two earlier guesses were wrong: ext/jdbc/ and apps/Data_Integration_Server/ext/drivers/ were both ignored by the connector. |
| CAI / process-engine JDBC driver | <agent>/apps/process-engine/ext — the Secure Agent picks jars up from here if you leave 'JDBC Jar Directory' blank. Otherwise set that field to any directory. | Vendor: IC_July2025_(JDBC)ConnectorGuide, ch.2. You must supply EITHER the jar directory OR the driver class name. |
| The directory only exists after the engine deploys | Do not pre-stage a driver before the engine lands — the path is created by deployment. Stage it, then restart the connector engine so it scans again. | Live: the driver was invisible until Connector_Service restarted. |
| Shaded-jar trap (ClickHouse, and any driver with a client split) | The `-all` classifier is NOT necessarily shaded. clickhouse-jdbc 0.6.5 `-all` omits com.clickhouse.client.* and throws NoClassDefFoundError ClickHouseClient. The correct artifact is **-shaded**. Verify with `unzip -l <jar> \| grep -c client/` before trusting it. | Live. A wrong download also returned a 554-byte HTML 404 page named .jar — always check the size. |
| JDBC_V2 sends NO password | The plugin XML declares HASUSERNAME="NO" HASUSERPASSWORD="NO" — there are no credential fields. Credentials in the URL, in userinfo form, or in additionalSecurityProperties were all stripped or ignored; the server saw the username but never a password. Read the plugin XML in downloads/package-JDBC_V2*/package/rdtm/plugins/*.xml — it is the authoritative field list. | Live, proven from both ends: the same URL forms all worked from a plain java -cp test, and ClickHouse's own log showed no-password auth. |

### Sizing the Secure Agent host

| Signal | Observed | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Engine JVM heap reservations | Enabling ALL services put 23 engines on one host whose -Xmx values summed to ~9.2 GB — more RAM than the 7.8 GiB machine had. | Sum the -Xmx of what you enable BEFORE clicking. Budget >=16 GB once Data Integration is on. |
| What over-subscription looks like | 27 OOM-kill events; the Linux OOM killer killed clickhouse-server twice plus mongod; load average 54 on 4 cores; engines flapping RUNNING->STOPPED; root disk 79% -> 95%. | Never co-locate a full engine set with production databases on a small host. Add swap — with none, every spike goes straight to the OOM killer. |
| Disk appetite | ~/infaagent grew to 25 GB, 19 GB of it installer packages under downloads/. | Keep ~20 GB free. Installer dirs under downloads/ do NOT map onto apps/ names, so they cannot be safely bulk-deleted by name match mid-deployment. |
| A governance-only engine set | Data_Integration_Server + Connector_Service + Metadata_Foundation_Agent + Metadata_Platform_Service ran fine (8 engines, 6 RUNNING) after trimming; load fell 65 -> 14. | Untick the rest: At_Scale_Server, B2BProcessor, CIHProcessor, DVProcessor, Database_Ingestion, MassIngestionRuntime, PC2CDI_Modernization_App, Streaming_Ingestion_Agent, ApiMicrogatewayService, AIAgentRuntime, DAM x2. |

## UI receipts — proof a UI-only action committed

For the 14 walls with no REST verb, the console's confirmation text is the only
machine-checkable proof the click committed. **USER-CAPTURED evidence — never invent one.**
An absent row means nobody has pasted it yet, not that the dialog is silent.

| Wall / action | UI path | Confirmation text | Substitutes for | Verify it landed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent service / engine enablement | Administrator → Runtime Environments → <agent> → edit components / services | "Changes successful. The selected components are enabled for the runtime environment, and all unselected components are disabled for the runtime environment." | POST /api/v2/agent/service → 403 APP_13401 / 500 CMN_001 (both are router artifacts — they prove nothing either way). POST /api/v2/agent/{id} with agentEngines[] → 500 and a silent no-op on read-back. | GET /api/v2/agent/details/{agentId} → agentEngines[] grows, each with agentEngineStatus.status DEPLOYING then RUNNING. Confirmed live 2026-07-26: 1 engine → 23 (9 RUNNING incl. Data_Integration_Server 77.0.2, Connector_Service 21.0.2). On-host: ls ~/infaagent/apps/ gains a directory per engine. |
| CDI mapping design | Mapping Designer canvas | UNCAPTURED |
| Taskflow publish | DI designer Publish click | UNCAPTURED |
| Mass Ingestion authoring | Mass Ingestion wizard | UNCAPTURED |
| CDQ rule + scorecard authoring | rulebuilder + DQO wizard | UNCAPTURED |
| CLAIRE classification accept | auto-accept threshold + re-scan | UNCAPTURED |
| MDM business-entity deploy | Business 360 Modeler Publish | UNCAPTURED |
| MDM ingress / match-merge run | B360 Console click | UNCAPTURED |
| Glossary term to column binding | CDGC UI | UNCAPTURED |
| Steward / data-owner assignment | CDGC UI | UNCAPTURED |
| Marketplace delivery template | Marketplace UI, headed browser | UNCAPTURED |
| DAM masking policy | Data Access Management UI | UNCAPTURED |
| Connector type registration | one UI Save in Administrator | UNCAPTURED |
| CDQ dictionary Convert to API | Data Quality → dictionary → Convert to API | UNCAPTURED |
| Sub-org license allocation | parent → Sub-Organizations → Licenses | UNCAPTURED |

**Still uncaptured (14):** CDI mapping design, Taskflow publish, Mass Ingestion authoring, CDQ rule + scorecard authoring, CLAIRE classification accept, MDM business-entity deploy, MDM ingress / match-merge run, Glossary term to column binding, Steward / data-owner assignment, Marketplace delivery template, DAM masking policy, Connector type registration, CDQ dictionary Convert to API, Sub-org license allocation.

⚠️ **A confirmation is not a completion.** After an enablement toast, engines sit in
`DEPLOYING` for 20+ minutes while packages download, and calls keep failing meanwhile with
errors that **change** between attempts. A shifting error is progress, not a new wall —
re-read the verify column before concluding the UI action failed. Enabling many services at
once can also fill the agent host's disk; check free space first.

## Not mounted on Org A

Proven-live on Org B, **absent on Org A** — borrowing these across orgs is the
single most common wrong answer this corpus records.

| Host / plane | On Org A |
|---|---|
| `<pod>-dqcloud-api` (CDQ dictionaries) | **404, not mounted** |
| `<pod>-mdm` (`/business-360`, MDM SaaS) | **404, not mounted** |
| `idmc-api` / `cdgc-api` (`data360/*`) | **zero-byte 200** — mounted, not serving (Law 2) |
| `<pod>-apigw` (`/apim`) | **503** — routed, nothing behind it |
| `GET /public/core/v3/mcpServers` | **404** — no vendor MCP server reachable |
| `mdm.<domain>` (unprefixed) | **DNS failure** — this form does not exist |

Org A planes that ARE live: `<pod>.dmp-us/saas` (v2 + v3 platform), `<pod>-cai`
(`/active-bpel`, 200 JSON), `<pod>-dqprofile` (`/profiling-service`, 200 JSON).
